alerts.title: Carbamazepine Reduces DTG Levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70%. The patient is on DTG-based ART (TLD) and started carbamazepine two weeks ago. The viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL with reported good adherence, suggesting a potential drug-drug interaction as the cause. The clinician's plan to reduce carbamazepine dose may help, but does not address the compromised ART efficacy.

evidence.recommended_action: Address the DTG-carbamazepine interaction. Consider alternative antiepileptic per guidelines or adjust ART regimen.

alerts.title: Viral Load >50 Copies/mL Requires Action
alerts.message: Guidelines for patients on DTG-based ART specify a viral load (VL) action threshold of >50 copies/mL. The patient's VL is 1,240 copies/mL. The recommended response is to provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects affecting adherence, and repeat VL in 2-3 months. The clinician's plan does not include these specific adherence interventions.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support and repeat viral load in 2-3 months as per the guideline algorithm.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine Toxicity with Hyponatremia
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms (nystagmus, ataxia, tremor) and a level (14 mcg/mL) consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. Hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also a known side effect of carbamazepine. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate. However, the hyponatremia should be monitored and managed.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose, repeat level, and monitor/manage hyponatremia.
